_doc: Per-agent model routing (mission 2026-07-05). Two layers, honestly separated: (1) claudeTier = the Claude model the subagent RUNS on (Agent-tool `model` param; aligns with FORGE_MODEL_ROUTING.json); (2) nvidia = which NVIDIA role-model (from model-capability-matrix.json roles) the agent calls AS A TOOL (via forge-bin/nvidia-provider.cjs) for LLM-work inside its task — drafts, summaries, classification, bulk generation, second-opinion review, vision. Claude-FIRST is the default (see usagePolicy below): NVIDIA is bulk-offload-only and is HARD-BLOCKED in code for the claudeWinsSkipNvidia Bosses; premium stays premium — never silently downgrade the premium/claude layer because an NVIDIA model exists. If NVIDIA is down/no-key/unsuitable → fallbackBehavior.
_wp15_note: WP 1.5 (2026-10-24): LEGACY MIRROR. The agent .md frontmatter is now the single source of truth for every per-agent fact; .claude/config/agents/agents.generated.json is generated from it (node .claude/forge-bin/forge-registry-gen.cjs agents --write) and forge-doctor `agents` cross-checks this file against it. This file stays, kept consistent, until a later wave removes it: change the agent frontmatter first, then this mirror, then regenerate. Cross-checked here (forge-policy routingCheck): claudeTier/claudeEffort == frontmatter model/effort. The NVIDIA-as-tool columns are a separate axis that only lives here.
fallbackBehavior: Adapter without key or on repeated failure → mock/off mode; the agent simply does the work itself on its Claude runtime model (labeled 'nvidia-skipped'). Never fake an NVIDIA response; never block work because NVIDIA is unavailable.

usagePolicy._verdict: NVIDIA-as-tool is BULK-OFFLOAD-ONLY (evidence: NVIDIA-vs-Claude comparison 2026-07-07). The Claude subagent is ALREADY running, so calling NVIDIA only pays off when it offloads genuinely BULK, LOW-RISK, high-volume output on a SEPARATE budget — never for quality-critical work. Default posture = Claude does it itself (nvidia-skipped).

claudeWinsSkipNvidia.why: Reasoning/planning: Opus is Anthropic's strongest reasoning tier (historical Opus 4.8 benchmark: HLE 49.8% vs kimi 36.4%; SWE-Verified 88.6% / SWE-Pro 69.2%, ~4x fewer missed flaws vs mistral-large-3 (mid-tier) — not yet re-measured for the current Opus 5.5, but the model class still leads). Security/integration: high-risk, errors costly. Vision: adapter is text-only + Claude leads OSWorld. For all these, Claude already-running is better AND cheaper (no extra hop) → skip NVIDIA.

nvidiaForBulkOnly.why: NVIDIA earns its place ONLY on bulk sub-tasks: first-draft docs, metadata/audit first-pass, source pre-summarization, registry/mapping validation, bulk test-fixture generation, and mechanical scaffolding/CRUD/DTO codegen — always on a separate budget and, for any code, behind the mandatory Forge build+test verification gate. The substantive part of each role still runs on Claude.

usagePolicy.codingNote: Claude Sonnet 5/Opus (current: Opus 5.5; historical 77-82% SWE-Verified measured on Opus 4.8, not yet re-measured for 5.5) >> gpt-oss-120b (62.4%). Real implementation/refactors/hard bugs stay on Claude; gpt-oss-120b only for mechanical high-volume codegen behind the build+test gate.

boss.why: GOAT deep route (opus, xhigh): the deep-route mission owner, dispatched for mission planning or deep packages — NOT the Lead (the main session is the sonnet router; Head Chef triages). Escalation follows the verifier-driven GOAT ladder (one retry: more effort first, then a bigger model; a second FAIL stops). NVIDIA is only a light in-task tool (fast working model) for long-context digestion/summaries; the slow 'reasoning' (Ultra) model would stall the mission.

head-chef.why: GOAT triage route (sonnet, low): adds {route, risk, checks} to every work package; read-only classification, not deep planning (that is Boss on the deep route). NVIDIA reasoning (kimi-k2.6) only as an in-task decomposition aid.

review-boss.why: Final QA must be strong (user rule: no weak cheap model). NVIDIA review model only as an EXTRA second opinion, never the sole verdict.

test-boss.why: Test planning/generation is coding work; Playwright execution is tooling, not model.

ui-boss.fallbackNote: NVIDIA vision is NOT usable today: the adapter sends TEXT ONLY (no image blocks) and the live multimodal models (qwen3.5-397b/122b) hang. So UI Boss's real screenshot/image analysis runs on its CLAUDE runtime (Sonnet/Opus receive images via the Agent tool). NVIDIA may still do TEXT-only UI reasoning via 'default'. Revisit when the adapter gains image support + a non-hanging vision model.
ui-boss.why: Screenshot/UI analysis needs images → Claude runtime (which gets them); NVIDIA text-only otherwise.

seo-boss.why: Structured audit work — solid general model, not creative-only.

security-boss.why: Security is high risk → Opus runtime (hardTasksAlwaysOpus); NVIDIA only as an extra reasoning lens (kimi-k2.6, best working reasoner — sharp on code-security in probe), never the sole verdict. The live safety sidecar nvidia/nemotron-content-safety-reasoning-4b may classify jailbreak/unsafe-content but is NOT the code-security judge.

search-boss.why: Source-grounded research; real search tools do the finding, model does synthesis.

build-boss.why: GOAT build route (opus · medium): implementation → coding-capable models only (user rule) — fallback stays coding-capable too. Hard/risky packages are triaged deep up front; Escalation follows the verifier-driven GOAT ladder (one retry: more effort first, then a bigger model; a second FAIL stops).

integration-boss.why: GOAT build route (opus · medium): API/error-handling integration work; auth/data-model packages are triaged deep (opus · xhigh) up front. Escalation follows the verifier-driven GOAT ladder (one retry: more effort first, then a bigger model; a second FAIL stops).

docs-boss.why: GOAT quick route (sonnet · low): docs are cheap/fast work; complex architecture/security docs are triaged build/deep. Escalation follows the verifier-driven GOAT ladder (one retry: more effort first, then a bigger model; a second FAIL stops).

data-scientist.why: 2026-09-26 registration (laptop re-audit D column): EDA-to-model implementation work. GOAT build route (opus · medium); high-stakes modeling/validation packages are triaged deep. Escalation follows the verifier-driven GOAT ladder (one retry: more effort first, then a bigger model; a second FAIL stops). Not in the curated nvidiaForBulkOnly bucket above — default posture applies (Claude does the substantive work itself).

electron-pro.why: 2026-09-26 registration: Electron packaging/IPC hardening is implementation work. GOAT build route (opus · medium); security-sensitive context-isolation/IPC design is triaged deep. Escalation follows the verifier-driven GOAT ladder (one retry: more effort first, then a bigger model; a second FAIL stops).

mcp-developer.why: 2026-09-26 registration: builds/debugs MCP servers and clients. GOAT build route (opus · medium); schema/security-sensitive tool-exposure decisions are triaged deep. Escalation follows the verifier-driven GOAT ladder (one retry: more effort first, then a bigger model; a second FAIL stops).

ml-engineer.why: 2026-09-26 registration: training-to-serving ML pipeline work is implementation-heavy. GOAT build route (opus · medium); drift/rollout-safety decisions are triaged deep. Escalation follows the verifier-driven GOAT ladder (one retry: more effort first, then a bigger model; a second FAIL stops).

payment-integration.why: 2026-09-26 registration: payment/webhook integration is high-risk implementation. GOAT deep route (opus · xhigh) by default (payments are deep work). Escalation follows the verifier-driven GOAT ladder (one retry: more effort first, then a bigger model; a second FAIL stops).

codex-reviewer.why: 2026-09-26 registration: optional external second-opinion reviewer — the real independent opinion is the pinned OpenAI Codex model it calls via Bash/PowerShell (config/orchestration/codex-review.json); Claude's own runtime only needs enough judgment to invoke it correctly and summarize the verdict, so it stays Opus-class without adding an NVIDIA hop for the core task.

verify-boss.why: 2026-09-26 registration: independent re-executor — reads a cold diff correctly and reports a literal exit code; needs strong judgment to avoid a false CONFIRMED/REFUTED call, but its core function is executing the real command, not an NVIDIA-offloadable task.

scribe.why: 2026-10-10 registration: GOAT quick route (sonnet · low). Classifying/linking owner requests is structured bookkeeping driven by forge-scribe.cjs; the deterministic tool does the enforcement, the model only reads the digest and runs the CLI. Dispatched rarely (multi_ask prompt, end-of-run reconciliation, resume with 20+ open items).

validation: Before dispatch: warn/block when an agent's assigned model violates 'prohibited' or the task clearly exceeds the model's caps (e.g. vision task on a non-vision model, implementation on a non-coding model). The adapter's `route <agent>` command resolves + validates this map against the capability matrix.
_effortNote: claudeTier + claudeEffort (GOAT model routing, 2026-10-06 — supersedes the 2026-07-12 note): documentation MIRROR of the native `model:` / `effort:` frontmatter in .claude/agents/<agent>.md and of the `model` field in agent-tool-policy.json — all three must agree. Every agent now has an explicit effort. Values = the agent's DEFAULT GOAT route (FORGE_MODEL_ROUTING.json → routes): head-chef = triage (sonnet/low); verify-boss, test-boss, codex-reviewer = verifier (sonnet/medium); docs/skill/search/seo-boss, scribe = quick (sonnet/low); build/ui/integration-boss, data-scientist, electron-pro, mcp-developer, ml-engineer = build (opus/medium); boss, review-boss, security-boss, payment-integration = deep (opus/xhigh). Haiku is no longer a default for any agent. Fable is never a default — only the escalate step (fable/high) after a failed Verify Boss check. Per dispatch the Lead passes the route model via the Agent-tool `model` param (overrides frontmatter); a non-default route effort is passed with the Agent-tool `effort` param or a Workflow agent({agentType, model, effort}) (updated 2026-11-01: Claude Code 2.1.292 added the Agent-tool `effort` param, installed 2.1.316; before that only a Workflow could set it). `premium` is unchanged (NVIDIA-tool routing, separate axis).
